hints: Resolve all forces along the horizontal and vertical axes.
Notice the vertical symmetry: the two $50\text{ N}$ forces have equal and opposite vertical components $50\sin\alpha - 50\sin\alpha = 0$.
Calculate the net horizontal force taking left as positive: $100 - 2(50)\cos\alpha$, and substitute $\cos\alpha = \frac{4}{5}$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces horizontally, taking the direction of the $100\text{ N}$ force (to the left) as positive:
$$R_x = 100 - 50\cos\alpha - 50\cos\alpha = 100 - 2(50)\cos\alpha$$

Resolve forces vertically perpendicular to the line of the $100\text{ N}$ force:
$$R_y = 50\sin\alpha - 50\sin\alpha = 0\text{ N}$$

State the resultant magnitude and direction:
$$\text{Magnitude} = 20\text{ N}, \quad \text{Direction is to the left (along the line of the } 100\text{ N force)}$$
teacher_walkthrough: Set up coordinate axes with the positive $x$-axis directed to the left along the $100\text{ N}$ force, and the $y$-axis directed vertically upwards.

State the formula for resolving the forces into their orthogonal components:
$$R_x = \sum F_x, \quad R_y = \sum F_y$$

Resolve the forces vertically. The two $50\text{ N}$ forces act symmetrically above and below the horizontal:
$$R_y = 50\sin\alpha - 50\sin\alpha = 0\text{ N}$$
Because the vertical components cancel completely, the resultant force is entirely horizontal.

Resolve the forces horizontally. The $100\text{ N}$ force acts to the left, while each $50\text{ N}$ force has a component of $50\cos\alpha$ directed to the right:
$$R_x = 100 - 2(50)\cos\alpha$$
Substitute the given value $\cos\alpha = \frac{4}{5}$ directly:
$$R_x = 100 - 2(50)\left(\frac{4}{5}\right) = 100 - 100\left(\frac{4}{5}\right) = 100 - 80 = 20\text{ N}$$

Conclude with the magnitude and direction:
$$\text{Resultant magnitude} = 20\text{ N}$$
$$\text{Direction} = \text{to the left (in the direction of the } 100\text{ N force)}$$
